anchors.paper_title: Neural Fragility as an EEG Marker of the Seizure Onset Zone
anchors.reason: The 2019 neural fragility preprint (91 patients) is a subset study the README says was "featured"; the dataset's own paper is Bernabei & Li et al. (in preparation), so it isn't the data paper.

anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiological data into BIDS, used to prepare the dataset, not a paper describing this iEEG dataset.

anchors.paper_title: iEEG-BIDS, extending the Brain Imaging Data Structure specification to human intracranial electrophysiology
anchors.reason: iEEG-BIDS is a specification for organizing intracranial EEG data, which this BIDS-formatted iEEG dataset uses; it does not describe this dataset itself.

anchors.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
anchors.reason: EEG-BIDS is a data-organization standard extending BIDS that this dataset's format follows; it does not describe the epilepsy iEEG multicenter data.

metadata.methods_description: Raw EDF files were converted to BrainVision format with MNE-BIDS. Clinicians marked electrodes anatomically for SEEG patients, and channels in white matter, ventricle, CSF or outside the brain were labeled as bad. Seizure onset and offset markers came from EDF annotations or clinician spreadsheets. Resected or ablated contacts were identified from surgical notes or by comparing postoperative MRI with CT scans.
